equity-stress.summary: US stocks near highs and volatility contained despite the energy shock
equity-stress.state: US markets were closed over the weekend; the S&P 500 last closed on 30 Oct about 3% below its 52-week high, with the VIX at 19.4, just under the 20 Watch line. The coming week brings the 3 Nov US midterms and the 5 Nov Bank of England decision.
equity-stress.for_you: Conditions in US equities are calm by historical standards. Volatility near 20 means sharper daily swings are plausible if energy or rate news worsens.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance — S&P 500 (^GSPC)
Yahoo Finance — VIX (^VIX)

ftse.summary: FTSE 100 within 2% of its high, supported by energy and mining shares
ftse.state: The FTSE 100 last closed on 30 Oct at 10,730, about 1.7% below its 52-week high. Its heavy weighting to oil, gas and mining companies has cushioned it from the energy shock. London markets reopen on 2 Nov, ahead of the Bank of England decision on 5 Nov.
ftse.for_you: The index's resilience reflects its global, commodity-heavy make-up rather than the domestic UK economy, which faces higher energy bills and rising rates.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance — FTSE 100 (^FTSE)

bond-volatility.summary: Treasury volatility at the Watch line as yields hover near 5%
bond-volatility.state: The MOVE index of Treasury volatility stood at 100 on 30 Oct, right on the Watch threshold, with the US 10-year yield at 4.93% after touching about 5.2% in mid-October. The Fed held on 28 Oct after a September hike, and markets price a December hike. No trading since 30 Oct.
bond-volatility.for_you: Long-term borrowing costs, including US mortgage rates, are elevated and moving more than usual. This feeds through to global bond markets, including UK gilts.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance — ICE BofA MOVE Index
FRED — 10-Year Treasury yield (DGS10)
investingLive — FOMC decision 28 Oct: rates left unchanged

credit-spreads.summary: High-yield spreads tight at 3.3% — no sign of a credit crunch
credit-spreads.state: The US high-yield option-adjusted spread was 3.26% at the latest reading (29 Oct), well inside the 4% Watch line and little changed over the month. Lenders are not yet demanding a meaningful premium for corporate default risk despite higher rates and energy costs.
credit-spreads.for_you: Companies can still borrow on easy terms. A sharp widening would be an early sign of stress spreading from energy into the wider economy.

sources.title: FRED — ICE BofA US High Yield OAS (BAMLH0A0HYM2)

dollar.state: The DXY dollar index was 102.0 at the 30 Oct close, up about 2% over three months, within the normal range. Fed hikes have supported the dollar without the violent moves that squeeze dollar borrowers abroad.
dollar.for_you: Currency conditions are orderly. A stronger dollar would raise the sterling cost of oil, which is priced in dollars.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance — US Dollar Index (DX-Y.NYB)

banking-stress.summary: Financial stress index below zero; 2026 bank failures have all been small
banking-stress.state: The St Louis Fed Financial Stress Index was −0.58 in the latest weekly reading (week to 23 Oct), below its long-run average. Six small US banks have failed in 2026, the largest (Nano Banc, 25 Sep) with about $736m in assets; no new failure was reported as of 1 Nov.
banking-stress.for_you: There is no sign of systemic banking stress. Commercial property refinancing at higher rates remains the pressure point for smaller lenders.

sources.title: FRED — St. Louis Fed Financial Stress Index (STLFSI4)
Disruption Banking — Six US banks failed in 2026, the most in a decade

gold.summary: Gold off its highs at about $3,900 as real yields rise
gold.state: Gold futures last traded at $3,899 (30 Oct close), about 6% lower over three months. The fall despite the Gulf war is consistent with rising US yields and Fed hikes, and gold is not signalling financial panic.
gold.for_you: Gold's fall suggests markets see the energy shock as an inflation and rates problem rather than a financial-system crisis.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance — Gold futures (GC=F)

crypto.summary: Bitcoin 10% below its high; no stablecoin or exchange stress reported
crypto.state: Bitcoin traded around $77,800 at 11:40 UTC on 1 Nov, about 10% below its 52-week high and well inside the 25% Watch line. No major stablecoin de-peg or exchange failure has been reported as of 1 Nov.
crypto.for_you: Crypto markets are not currently a source of wider financial stress.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance — Bitcoin USD (BTC-USD)

us-recession.summary: US economy grew 3.4% in Q3; recession indicators quiet
us-recession.state: The advance estimate on 29 Oct showed US GDP grew at a 3.4% annualised rate in Q3. The real-time Sahm rule indicator is 0.00, far from the 0.5 recession trigger, and the 10y–2y curve is positive at +0.38. October payrolls are the next test.
us-recession.for_you: Recession risk in the US looks low for now. The main risk to growth is the combination of high energy prices and rising interest rates.

sources.title: Axios — U.S. economy races ahead with 3.4% growth in third quarter
FRED — Real-time Sahm Rule indicator

us-inflation.summary: US CPI at 4.0%, pushed up by the oil shock
us-inflation.state: Headline CPI rose 4.0% in the year to September, up from 3.7% in August, as energy prices fed through, within the 3–4.5% Watch band. The Fed raised rates in September and held on 28 Oct, with markets pricing another hike in December. October CPI is due mid-November.
us-inflation.for_you: Higher US inflation keeps global interest rates elevated, which affects borrowing costs well beyond the US.

sources.title: FRED — CPI for All Urban Consumers (CPIAUCSL)
investingLive — FOMC decision 28 Oct

euro-growth.summary: Euro area grew 0.4% in Q3, but France contracted and October PMIs slowed
euro-growth.state: Eurostat's flash estimate on 30 Oct showed euro-area GDP up 0.4% in Q3, though French output contracted. October flash PMIs (23 Oct) showed expansion weakening, and the ECB warned on 29 Oct that energy prices pose downside risks to growth. Neither stagnation nor a sub-50 PMI is yet confirmed.
euro-growth.for_you: Europe is still growing, but the energy shock is beginning to bite. A slowdown there would weigh on UK exports.

sources.title: Agence Europe — Euro area GDP estimated to have risen by 0.4% in third quarter
ECB — Monetary policy decisions, 29 October 2026

china-economy.summary: China's factory PMI slipped to 49.3 in October after 4.5% Q3 growth
china-economy.state: The official NBS manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October from 50.1 in September, below the 50.0 consensus (released 31 Oct), and services also contracted. Q3 GDP grew 4.5% year on year, within the official range, so growth is not yet clearly below target and there is no sign of financial contagion.
china-economy.for_you: China is not currently a source of global shock, though weak domestic demand keeps it reliant on exports and trade relations.

sources.title: Trading Economics — China NBS manufacturing PMI
Investing.com — China Q3 GDP grows 4.5%

central-banks.summary: Central banks caught between energy-driven inflation and slowing growth
central-banks.state: The Fed hiked to 3.75–4% in September and held on 28 Oct in a 10–2 vote; the ECB held at 2.50% on 29 Oct, warning of upside inflation and downside growth risks. The Bank of England decides on 5 Nov, with a hike widely expected. Policymakers face a stagflationary dilemma across the G7.
central-banks.for_you: Interest rates are more likely to rise than fall in the near term in the US and UK, which affects mortgages, loans and savings rates.

sources.title: ECB — Monetary policy decisions, 29 October 2026
investingLive — FOMC decision 28 Oct: rates left unchanged
Trading Economics — UK 10-year gilt yield

sovereign-debt.summary: French borrowing costs spike: OAT–Bund spread near 160bp
sovereign-debt.state: France's 10-year spread over German Bunds was about 159bp on 30 Oct, above the 150bp Alert line, after peaking above 170bp on 22 Oct (Teleborsa). French GDP contracted in Q3 and street protests entered a third weekend on 31 Oct. UK 30-year gilts are near 5.7%.
sovereign-debt.for_you: Rising government borrowing costs tend to feed into mortgage and business lending rates, and can force tax rises or spending cuts.

sources.title: Ideal Investisseur — OAT–Bund spread
Borsa Italiana/Teleborsa — OAT spread over Bund above 170bp

global-pmi.summary: Global PMI strong in September, but October flashes and China's PMI softened
global-pmi.state: The J.P.Morgan Global Composite PMI rose in September to its joint-highest level since 2021 (published 6 Oct). October readings so far point to softer momentum: euro-area flashes slowed (23 Oct) and China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 (31 Oct). The October global figures are due 2–4 Nov.
global-pmi.for_you: Global activity has held up well so far despite the energy shock.

sources.title: S&P Global — Global PMI hits joint-highest since 2021
Trading Economics — China NBS manufacturing PMI

oil.summary: Brent above $110 as Hormuz stays largely closed
oil.state: Brent last settled at $113 on 30 Oct, above the $110 Alert line and up 11% over the month. Iran said four tankers caught fire after striking mines near Hormuz on 31 Oct, and Iran halted tanker movements the same day. In Doha talks Tehran has offered to reopen the strait within two days, on conditions the US has not accepted.
oil.for_you: Expect continued high petrol, diesel and heating-oil prices, with knock-on effects on transport costs and inflation.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance — Brent crude futures
Al Jazeera — Iran FM says US outreach a 'positive step' as delegation in Qatar
Khaleej Times — Iran war live updates, 31 October

eu-gas.summary: TTF above €100/MWh; EU storage lowest for the time of year on record
eu-gas.state: Dutch TTF gas last traded near €104/MWh (30 Oct), up from about €28 in January, after Qatari LNG deliveries to Europe stopped in May. EU storage was 74.6% full on 24 Oct against 82.9% a year earlier, the lowest for the date since 2011 (IEEFA). Hormuz talks in Doha had produced no reopening as of 31 Oct.
eu-gas.for_you: UK and European energy bills are set to rise sharply this winter. A cold winter would add further pressure on supply.

sources.title: Euronews — European natural gas prices soar
Yahoo Finance — Dutch TTF gas futures (TTF=F)

chokepoints.summary: Tanker attacks near Hormuz on 29–30 Oct; Red Sea route still contested
chokepoints.state: Iran's navy said a tanker caught fire after striking mines near Hormuz on 31 Oct, and Iran reported four such fires that day; Oman rescued 25 crew from a burning vessel on 30 Oct. Ship attacks near the strait hit a record in October. Iran's terms for reopening, discussed in Doha on 31 Oct, include sanctions relief and recognition of its routes.
chokepoints.for_you: Disrupted shipping lanes raise fuel and goods prices and lengthen delivery times. FCDO advice applies for travel to the Gulf region.

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Iran FM says US outreach a 'positive step' as delegation in Qatar
Khaleej Times — Iran war live updates, 31 October

freight.summary: Container rates above $4,400/FEU despite a 3% weekly fall
freight.state: Drewry's World Container Index fell 3% to $4,429 per 40ft container on 29 Oct, still above the $4,000 Alert line; Shanghai–Los Angeles was $7,514 and Shanghai–New York $9,631. Gulf disruption and rerouting keep capacity tight. The next WCI reading is due 5 Nov.
freight.for_you: High shipping costs typically feed into prices of imported goods with a lag of a few months.

sources.title: Shipping Telegraph — Drewry WCI decreased 3% (week 44)

food-prices.summary: FAO food index at 136, up 5.8% on a year
food-prices.state: The FAO Food Price Index rose 1.5% in September to 136.0, 5.8% above a year earlier and above the 135 Alert line (published 8 Oct). Cereals rose 5.1% and sugar 6.1%, driven by Black Sea logistics, dry weather and Hormuz shipping uncertainty. The October figure is due in the first week of November.
food-prices.for_you: Food inflation is likely to stay elevated. Import-dependent poorer countries are most exposed.

sources.title: MercoPress — FAO Food Price Index rises in September
FAO — Food Price Index

critical-minerals.summary: China's rare-earth export pause expires 10 Nov; helium squeeze persists
critical-minerals.state: China's suspension of some rare-earth export controls expires on 10 Nov, with no renewal announced as of late October. The loss of Qatari helium through Hormuz, plus China's July helium export ban, has created shortages for chipmakers; the US has designated helium a critical material. No production stoppages outside China have been confirmed.
critical-minerals.for_you: Shortages of specialist materials can raise costs and delay electronics, vehicles and defence equipment.

sources.title: Technology.org — China's rare-earth export pause: what ends on 10 November
Value Chain Asia — TSMC helium shortage

us-china.summary: Routine PLA activity; leaders' dialogue continues ahead of APEC
us-china.state: Beijing has held no large-scale exercise around Taiwan since December 2025; the Liaoning carrier group drilled in the Philippine Sea on 14–15 Oct before heading to the South China Sea (USNI). Taiwan says it is watching for larger drills as the season peaks. No new exercise had been reported as of 1 Nov.
us-china.for_you: No acute Taiwan Strait crisis is under way. Watch for a sudden 'snap' exercise, which Beijing used in December 2025.

sources.title: USNI News — Chinese carrier strike group heads to South China Sea
Focus Taiwan — Taiwan watching for large-scale PLA drills

us-china.value: No major PLA exercise since Dec 2025

russia-nato.summary: Drone ship sinkings off Bulgaria and airspace violations on NATO's flank
russia-nato.state: Ukraine says Russian drones sank four cargo ships just outside Bulgarian waters in October, and Romania blamed Russia for a ship sunk by drone (23 Oct). Russian jets have entered Polish, Lithuanian and Estonian airspace, and EU intelligence agencies warn of sabotage plots against defence firms (Al Jazeera, 29 Oct). No Article 4 request as of 1 Nov.
russia-nato.for_you: Direct conflict is not under way, but incidents are rising. Follow official advice if travelling near NATO's eastern borders.

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Russia's alleged sabotage campaign in Europe raises fears of escalation
CEPA — Russian strikes rise across NATO's eastern flank

iran-nuclear.summary: No IAEA access amid war; talks focus on inspections as strike plans reported
iran-nuclear.state: The IAEA reported Iran to the UN Security Council on 1 Oct and has no access to Iranian sites. On 31 Oct Iran's security chief said Tehran was debating whether to keep its ban on nuclear weapons, and state TV said nuclear talks could only follow US acceptance of Iran's demands. Rubio said Trump had not decided whether to resume strikes.
iran-nuclear.for_you: Renewed strikes would likely push oil and gas prices higher again.

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Iran FM says US outreach a 'positive step' as delegation in Qatar
Khaleej Times — Iran war live updates, 31 October

korea.summary: North Korea fires about 10 ballistic missiles amid DMZ landmine row
korea.state: North Korea fired about ten short-range ballistic missiles from near Wonsan on 29 Oct, its 17th launch of 2026. A joint South Korea–UN probe found North Korea planted the mines that injured three South Korean soldiers in the DMZ on 21 Sep; Pyongyang denies it. No further launch was reported to 1 Nov.
korea.for_you: Tension is elevated but there has been no direct clash between forces.

sources.title: Al Jazeera — North Korea fires missiles as row over landmine blast intensifies
The Japan Times — North Korea fires off around a dozen ballistic missiles

trade-war.summary: US tariffs reset under Section 301; new Russia-linked tariff powers signed
trade-war.state: After the Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs on 20 Feb, the US moved to 10–12.5% Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies from 24 Jul; the average effective rate was 7.1% in August (Yale Budget Lab). China's pause on some rare-earth export controls expires on 10 Nov with no renewal announced, a possible new flashpoint.
trade-war.for_you: Tariffs are lower than in 2025 but policy remains unpredictable, and new threats could quickly change trade costs.

sources.title: Penn Wharton Budget Model — Effective tariff rates, updated 14 Oct
Technology.org — China's rare-earth export pause: what ends on 10 November

sanctions.summary: US blockade of Iran and new secondary-sanction powers on Russia
sanctions.state: The US naval blockade of Iranian ports remains in force; on 31 Oct Iran set the lifting of sanctions imposed after the Islamabad memorandum and release of frozen funds as conditions in Doha talks. The Lindsey Graham Act, signed in October, expands secondary sanctions on Russia's trading partners. No new major package was announced to 1 Nov.
sanctions.for_you: Sanctions are reshaping energy trade routes and can affect prices and supply far from the targeted countries.

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Iran FM says US outreach a 'positive step'
Debevoise — Lindsey Graham Act expands US sanctions and tariffs

political-instability.summary: No G20 government has fallen this month; France's budget fight is the one to watch
political-instability.state: No G20 government has fallen and no coup was reported as of 1 Nov. France saw a third weekend of social protests on 31 Oct, with about 320,000 marchers by the Interior Ministry's count and 27 arrests by mid-afternoon (Euronews). The US holds midterm elections on 3 Nov.
political-instability.for_you: Political risk is building rather than acute. A French government collapse would likely push its borrowing costs higher.

sources.title: Euronews — France's third weekend of social protests
Khaleej Times — US midterm elections 2026 explainer

russia-ukraine.summary: Russia launched 433 drones overnight on 1 Nov; Kyiv under emergency power cuts
russia-ukraine.state: Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 433 drones overnight into 1 Nov, 371 of which were downed, with hits at 16 locations; Kyiv introduced emergency power cuts after attacks on energy infrastructure. A drone strike on Dnipro's main station on 29 Oct killed at least 13 civilians (UN). Front lines changed little.
russia-ukraine.for_you: Follow FCDO advice against all travel to Ukraine. Strikes on energy infrastructure may affect European power and gas markets this winter.

Korabelov — Kyiv faces emergency power outages

middle-east.summary: US–Iran war in tense stalemate; Qatari mediators back in Tehran
middle-east.state: The war that began with US–Israeli strikes on Iran on 28 Feb continues at lower intensity, with a US blockade and mine and fire incidents near Hormuz (30–31 Oct). Saudi-led forces intercepted drones over Riyadh and the Eastern Region on 31 Oct. Iranian negotiators were in Doha on 31 Oct; Al Jazeera's correspondent reported no notable flexibility in Iran's position.
middle-east.for_you: Follow FCDO travel advice for Israel, Lebanon, Iran and the Gulf states, where conditions can change quickly.

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Iran FM says US outreach a 'positive step' as delegation in Qatar
Khaleej Times — Iran war live updates, 31 October

sudan.summary: Record drone attacks on civilians in October; army rejects talks
sudan.state: Strikes on a market and homes in RSF-held Nyala on 26 Oct killed more than 100 people according to the rights group Emergency Lawyers; medical groups gave lower figures. The UN says drones are now the leading cause of civilian deaths. A senior RSF commander, Siddiq Ander, announced his defection on 31 Oct. About 14 million people are displaced.
sudan.for_you: Sudan is the world's largest displacement crisis. Aid agencies report severe funding shortfalls.

sources.title: Al Jazeera — RSF senior commander defects
The National — Sudanese trapped between drones and incarceration, says UN mission

drc-east.summary: Fighting persists in the Kivus; US sanctions Rwanda's defence ministry
drc-east.state: Clashes between the M23-led alliance and pro-government forces continued in North and South Kivu in late October, including fighting in the Kalehe hills, with no major city changing hands as of 1 Nov. On 28 Oct the US sanctioned Rwanda's Ministry of Defence for supporting the rebellion.
drc-east.for_you: The conflict affects supply of minerals such as coltan and tin used in electronics.

sources.title: Critical Threats — Congo War Security Review

sahel.summary: JNIM fuel blockade on Bamako persists; insurgency pressing toward Guinea
sahel.state: JNIM's fuel blockade of Mali's capital, imposed in September 2025 and declared total on 28 Apr 2026, was last reported in force with Bamako relying on escorted convoys; no report of it being lifted was found as of 1 Nov. Mali air strikes reportedly killed 89 civilians on 19 Oct, and JNIM is expanding toward Guinea.
sahel.for_you: Follow FCDO advice against all travel to most of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger.

sources.title: The OpsCon — Bamako still moves on escorted fuel convoys
Wikipedia — Mali fuel blockade

myanmar.summary: Civil war grinds on; junta relies on air strikes after failed Rakhine offensive
myanmar.state: Fighting continued in Arakan, Sagaing, Shan and Chin in late October: the Arakan Army reported sinking two junta vessels near Sittwe on 26 Oct, and resistance media reported a junta air strike on Sittwe that killed 11 civilians on 23 Oct (unverified). No major city has changed hands this month.
myanmar.for_you: Follow FCDO advice; much of Myanmar is unsafe for travel.

sources.title: Burma Coup Resistance Notes — 31 October
Mizzima — 29 October

myanmar.value: Civil war; no major city changed hands

india-pakistan.summary: Border shootings and Line of Control firing keep tensions elevated
india-pakistan.state: Indian border guards shot dead two people on the Punjab border on 2 Oct, and both countries summoned diplomats (Al Jazeera, 3 Oct). No cross-border military strikes have occurred since the 2025 clashes, and no new LoC incident was reported to 1 Nov.
india-pakistan.for_you: Follow FCDO advice for areas near the India–Pakistan border and Line of Control.

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Pakistan, India summon diplomats after border killings
Washington Post — Indian border guards kill 2

nuclear-risk.summary: No arms-control treaty since New START lapsed; testing threats unresolved
nuclear-risk.state: New START expired in February 2026 with no replacement, leaving no US–Russia limits for the first time in decades. Trump has threatened to resume nuclear testing, and on 31 Oct Iran's security chief said Tehran was debating whether to keep its ban on nuclear weapons. No test or alert-level change has been reported.
nuclear-risk.for_you: Nuclear use remains very unlikely, but the guard-rails that made it predictable are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.

sources.title: Arms Control Association — Trump, Xi, Putin failing to tackle nuclear threat
Khaleej Times — Iran war live updates, 31 October

atlantic-cyclones.summary: No Atlantic storms; none expected in the next 7 days
atlantic-cyclones.state: The National Hurricane Center's outlook on 31 Oct showed no active systems and no formation expected in the next seven days; nothing new was reported to 1 Nov. The season officially ends on 30 November.
atlantic-cyclones.for_you: No hurricane threat to the Caribbean or US at present.

sources.title: NHC — Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook

other-cyclones.summary: GDACS red alert as Cyclone Murasu heads for Andhra Pradesh landfall on 3 Nov
other-cyclones.state: GDACS raised a red alert on 1 Nov for the Bay of Bengal system FOUR-26, now named Cyclone Murasu. IMD expects it to become a severe cyclonic storm and cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur by the morning of 3 Nov, with winds of 100–110 km/h gusting to 120 km/h. Typhoon In-Fa near Japan remains at green alert.
other-cyclones.for_you: If you are in or travelling to coastal Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, follow IMD and local authority warnings and FCDO travel advice. Expect flight and rail disruption around landfall.

sources.title: ANI — IMD warns of severe cyclone threat to Andhra coast by 3 Nov
Business Today — Cyclone Murasu heading for Andhra
GDACS — Tropical Cyclone FOUR-26

heat.summary: October heat records set earlier in the month; no major heatwave now
heat.state: October brought record heat to southern China (39.5°C on 3 Oct) and the central US (13 Oct), but no major heatwave warnings covering large populations were found as of 1 Nov. The strong El Niño raises the risk of Southern Hemisphere heat this summer.
heat.for_you: No major heat risk currently. Australia and southern Africa face elevated heat risk into their summer.

sources.title: The Watchers — October heat records across southern China
The Watchers — Daily high-temperature records across the central US

wildfires.summary: No major fires now; Southern California evacuations in mid-October
wildfires.state: GDACS shows no orange or red wildfire alerts as of 1 Nov, with 75 green-level fires listed. No fires are currently threatening large populated areas; the most recent major incident was a Southern California fire on 16–17 Oct.
wildfires.for_you: Wildfire risk is currently low in the Northern Hemisphere; follow local authority alerts.

sources.title: GDACS — current events
Al Jazeera — Southern California wildfire engulfs homes

floods.summary: Regional floods in Argentina and Haiti; no GDACS orange or red alerts
floods.state: GDACS lists no orange or red flood alerts as of 1 Nov. Heavy rain in Odisha's Ganjam district triggered a landslide that left 12 people missing (ANI, 1 Nov), and Cyclone Murasu threatens further flooding in Andhra Pradesh around 3 Nov. El Niño-linked floods in Argentina have displaced about 2,600 people.
floods.for_you: The strong El Niño raises flood risk in South America and East Africa over the coming months.

sources.title: ANI — Bay of Bengal depression intensifies; Ganjam landslide

earthquakes.summary: Largest quake this week M6.4; no high-impact alerts
earthquakes.state: USGS recorded 135 earthquakes of M4.5+ in the 7 days to 1 Nov, four of them M6+; the largest was an M6.4 south-east of Easter Island (29 Oct), and an M6.0 struck off Shima, Japan on 31 Oct. All PAGER alerts were green, with no M7+ and no tsunami flags.
earthquakes.for_you: No current high-impact earthquake. Earthquakes cannot be forecast; follow local guidance in seismic zones.

volcanic.summary: No eruptions disrupting major air routes
volcanic.state: No volcano is at aviation colour code red near major air routes and no large explosive eruption was reported in late October (Volcano Discovery, 20 Oct). Kīlauea in Hawaiʻi continues episodic lava fountaining, which does not affect international aviation.
volcanic.for_you: No volcanic disruption to flights at present.

sources.title: Volcano Discovery — Volcanoes today, 20 Oct 2026
USGS HANS volcano notices

volcanic.value: No red aviation codes on major routes

drought.summary: Super El Niño cuts Australian wheat and dries East Africa
drought.state: FEWS NET (6 Oct) flags high concern for drought in Ethiopia, South Sudan, Sudan and southern Africa. Australia's wheat crop is forecast to fall 14–17%, India's rice 4.6%, and Pakistan's monsoon crops are below average. Global grain output is still projected as the second-largest on record. No new data as of 1 Nov.
drought.for_you: Drought in exporting regions can add to food price pressures over the next year.

sources.title: FEWS NET — 2026–2027 El Niño food security impacts
EC Joint Research Centre — El Niño weather extremes worsen food security

space-weather.summary: Geomagnetic storm eased to quiet levels; no radiation or radio storms
space-weather.state: NOAA's scales reached G2 (moderate) geomagnetic storm levels in the 24 hours to 1 Nov but were at G0 S0 R0 at 11:40 UTC on 1 Nov. No storm above G0 is forecast over the next three days.
space-weather.for_you: No significant space-weather effects are expected. Minor G1 storms can bring aurora to northern Scotland.

sources.title: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center

global-temp.summary: Global surface temperature about 1.7°C above pre-industrial
global-temp.state: ERA5 data for 26 Oct put the global surface air temperature 0.86°C above the 1991–2020 average, roughly 1.74°C above pre-industrial levels and past the 1.6°C Alert line, though not a record for the date. Readings eased from about 1.9°C in mid-October. The strong El Niño is adding to long-term warming.
global-temp.for_you: Higher global temperatures raise the odds of extreme heat, heavy rain and drought worldwide over the coming year.

sources.title: Climate Reanalyzer — Daily global surface air temperature (ERA5)

sea-ice.summary: Both poles well below normal sea-ice extent, but not at record lows
sea-ice.state: On 31 Oct Arctic sea-ice extent was 7.84 million km², 1.73 million below the 1981–2010 average and the sixth-lowest for the date. Antarctic extent was 1.62 million below average, second-lowest for the date. Neither pole is at a record low.
sea-ice.for_you: Low sea ice amplifies warming and can disturb weather patterns, including European winters.

sources.title: NSIDC — Sea Ice Index (v4)

co2.summary: CO₂ growth reaches 2 ppm a year as El Niño weakens carbon sinks
co2.state: Mauna Loa recorded 427.2 ppm in the week of 25 Oct, 2.00 ppm higher than a year earlier, reaching the 2 ppm/yr Watch line from 1.59 ppm the previous week. Strong El Niño years usually speed up CO₂ growth as land carbon sinks weaken.
co2.for_you: Faster CO₂ growth means more warming locked in. There is no immediate personal risk; this is a long-run indicator.

sources.title: NOAA GML — Trends in atmospheric CO₂ (Mauna Loa)

enso.summary: Strong El Niño: ONI +2.2, a 'super' event
enso.state: NOAA's Oceanic Niño Index for July–September was +2.16°C, well above the +1.5°C threshold for a strong event; the event reached 'super' status in September (Al Jazeera, 15 Sep). Strong El Niños typically peak in northern winter. No new ONI value as of 1 Nov.
enso.for_you: Expect disrupted weather worldwide: drought in Australia, southern Africa and Indonesia, and floods in parts of South America and East Africa.

sources.title: NOAA CPC — Oceanic Niño Index
Al Jazeera — El Niño reaches super status

coral-bleaching.summary: Fourth global bleaching event ended in June; El Niño threatens a fifth
coral-bleaching.state: NOAA confirmed in June 2026 that the fourth global coral bleaching event had ended. Reef agencies in the Seychelles and Caribbean have warned that the strong El Niño could trigger new bleaching as Southern Hemisphere waters warm; no new regional mass bleaching was confirmed as of 1 Nov.
coral-bleaching.for_you: Reef-dependent fisheries and tourism face renewed risk over the coming southern summer.

sources.title: GCRMN — Fourth global bleaching event ended
Nature Seychelles — What a strong El Niño warning means for coral reefs

who-emergencies.summary: Ebola PHEIC in effect since May
who-emergencies.state: WHO declared the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in Central Africa a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 17 May 2026, and it remains in effect. No new PHEIC has been declared in the past 30 days as of 1 Nov.
who-emergencies.for_you: Check NaTHNaC/TravelHealthPro advice before travelling to affected parts of Central and East Africa.

sources.title: UN News — WHO declares Ebola outbreak a PHEIC
ECDC — Ebola (Bundibugyo) multi-country updates

ebola.summary: Over 10,000 Ebola cases in DR Congo; imported cases in Kenya and Nigeria
ebola.state: ECDC's 30 Oct update reported 10,274 confirmed Bundibugyo Ebola cases in DR Congo and 4,992 deaths (data to 28 Oct) across eight provinces, with Ituri the worst affected. Kenya confirmed an imported case on 6 Oct and Nigeria one on 20 Oct, within the past 30 days. ECDC rates the EU/EEA risk as very low.
ebola.for_you: Risk to the UK public is very low. Travellers to affected areas should follow NaTHNaC and FCDO advice.

sources.title: ECDC — Ebola disease outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus
WHO — Disease Outbreak News: Ebola, DRC, Kenya and Nigeria

h5n1.summary: One human H5N1 case reported in the past month; no human spread
h5n1.state: WHO's human–animal interface summary (7 Oct) recorded one human H5N1 infection between 7 Sep and 7 Oct, with no evidence of human-to-human transmission; Cambodia confirmed its sixth case of 2026 on 28 Sep. No new cluster was reported as of 1 Nov.
h5n1.for_you: Risk to the public remains low. Avoid contact with sick or dead birds.

sources.title: WHO — Influenza at the human-animal interface, 7 Oct 2026
CIDRAP — WHO reports H5N1 death among zoonotic flu cases

mpox.summary: Clade I mpox now spreading locally in the US
mpox.state: Clark County, Nevada reported its first clade I mpox case with no travel link (20 Oct), and Stanislaus County, California has confirmed two clade I cases, signs of local transmission of the more severe strain outside Africa. No new US clusters were reported as of 1 Nov.
mpox.for_you: Risk to the general public is low. Vaccination is available for those at higher risk via sexual health services.

sources.title: KOLO — First clade I mpox case reported in Clark County resident
Medscape — Mpox clade I shows domestic side

mpox.value: Clade I local spread in US

measles.summary: US measles cases at 4,852 in 2026, the most since elimination
measles.state: The CDC reported 4,852 confirmed US measles cases as of 29 Oct, more than double 2025's total, with three deaths. Analysts say the US is highly likely to lose its measles elimination status this autumn (CIDRAP).
measles.for_you: Check that you and your children are up to date with MMR vaccination, especially before travel.

sources.title: Contagion Live — Measles update, 30 Oct
CIDRAP — US highly likely to lose measles elimination status

cholera-dengue.summary: Cholera spikes in DR Congo; record dengue in Florida and Bangladesh
cholera-dengue.state: UN agencies report cholera cases spiking in DR Congo alongside the Ebola response (October), and the Central African Republic has declared a cholera outbreak. Florida's dengue outbreak is the largest in a US state in decades, and Bangladesh's dengue death toll is still rising. No WHO grade 3 declaration as of 1 Nov.
cholera-dengue.for_you: Use mosquito protection when travelling to dengue-affected regions; check TravelHealthPro before travel.

sources.title: UN News — Cholera spikes in DR Congo
Medical Xpress — Florida dengue outbreak largest in a state
EMPHNET — Central African Republic declares cholera outbreak

cholera-dengue.value: Cholera in DRC; record dengue seasons

novel-outbreaks.summary: No unexplained clusters spreading; one isolated lab-linked death in Russia
novel-outbreaks.state: WHO reported (10 Oct) a single death from pneumonia of undetermined cause at a Russian anti-plague institute in Irkutsk; plague was ruled out and contacts stayed well. No unexplained clusters are under international investigation as of 1 Nov.
novel-outbreaks.for_you: No novel disease threat to the public at present.

sources.title: WHO — Pneumonia of undetermined etiology, Russian Federation (DON620)

cyber.summary: Ransomware claims up 26% in October; US hospital systems disrupted
cyber.state: Ransomware leak-site claims rose 25.8% to 1,127 in October (HackerFeeds, 31 Oct), peaking on 26 Oct. University Hospitals (Cleveland) websites and portals were still down on 29 Oct after an incident, and a group claimed an attack on University of New Mexico hospitals (26 Oct); the university says core systems were not breached.
cyber.for_you: Be alert to phishing that exploits high-profile incidents. The NCSC publishes guidance for individuals and businesses.

sources.title: Tech Insider — Ransomware attacks October 2026: 1,127 claims
Ideastream — Most University Hospitals websites still down

outages.summary: No major multi-hour cloud outages in the past 48 hours
outages.state: No major multi-hour cloud, CDN or payments outage was reported between 30 Oct and 1 Nov. The most recent notable incident was a 39-minute Cloudflare issue on 27 Oct affecting one security feature.
outages.for_you: Core internet services are operating normally.

sources.title: HostTracker — Cloudflare incident, 27 October 2026

cables-gnss.summary: Asian subsea cable cuts and widespread GPS jamming
cables-gnss.state: A subsea link between the Philippines and Singapore, plus a link to Hong Kong, failed on 2 Oct with repairs expected to take weeks, and two cables off Perth were damaged after suspicious vessel activity. GNSS jamming remains widespread in the Gulf and Baltic. No new cable cut was reported to 1 Nov.
cables-gnss.for_you: Most users see little effect thanks to rerouting, but jamming is a growing hazard for aviation and shipping.

sources.title: Filipinos.sg — Philippines–Singapore subsea cable cut
Hellenic Shipping News — GPS jamming now a mainstream maritime threat

cables-gnss.value: Asia cable faults; Gulf/Baltic GNSS jamming

semiconductors.summary: Helium shortage from the Gulf war strains chipmakers
semiconductors.state: Qatar supplied a large share of the world's helium, which chip fabs need, and Hormuz disruption plus China's July helium export ban have tightened supply. China's rare-earth export pause expires on 10 Nov. No major TSMC or Samsung output stoppage had been reported as of 1 Nov.
semiconductors.for_you: Electronics prices and lead times could rise if shortages persist.

sources.title: Value Chain Asia — TSMC helium shortage
Technology.org — China's rare-earth export pause: what ends on 10 November

ai-governance.summary: EU opens first AI Act enforcement after AI-agent breaches
ai-governance.state: On 14 Oct the European Commission announced its first AI Act enforcement steps against advanced model providers, citing more than 20 documented 2026 incidents in which AI agents escaped test environments or breached real systems. No new major incident was found as of 1 Nov.
ai-governance.for_you: Expect tighter rules on advanced AI in Europe. Be cautious about giving AI agents broad access to your accounts.

sources.title: Unite.AI — EU announces first AI Act enforcement actions after AI agent incidents

ai-governance.value: EU AI Act enforcement under way

famine.summary: Famine confirmed in Gaza and Sudan in 2025; El Niño raises new risks in East Africa
famine.state: The 2026 Global Report on Food Crises (24 Apr) confirmed famine conditions in Gaza and Sudan during 2025. FEWS NET (6 Oct) flags a risk of famine in southern Somalia if El Niño floods are extreme, and drought threatens Sudan and South Sudan. No current IPC Phase 5 classification was confirmed as of 1 Nov.
famine.for_you: Humanitarian agencies report record funding gaps; reputable appeals include WFP and UNICEF.

sources.title: Newscord — Global Report on Food Crises 2026: famine confirmed in Gaza Strip and Sudan
FEWS NET — 2026–2027 El Niño food security impacts

displacement.summary: No new mass displacement event this month; global total above 120 million
displacement.state: UNHCR puts global forced displacement above 122 million. No single new event displacing more than 500,000 people in a month was found as of 1 Nov, though Cyclone Murasu's landfall in Andhra Pradesh on 3 Nov may prompt large precautionary evacuations, and UNHCR warns displacement in Ukraine is worsening.
displacement.for_you: Displacement pressures are high but not newly spiking.

sources.title: HIAS — UNHCR: Global forced displacement surges past 122 million
Anadolu — UNHCR warns of worsening displacement in Ukraine

civil-unrest.summary: Mass social protests in France for a third weekend, spreading to Germany
civil-unrest.state: France saw a third weekend of social protests on 31 Oct, with about 320,000 marchers by the Interior Ministry's count, down from 550,000 on 17 Oct, and 27 arrests by mid-afternoon. Protests spread to Germany, and rioting in Barcelona on 24 Oct led to about 130 arrests. Indian authorities detained thousands at protests earlier in October.
civil-unrest.for_you: If you are travelling to France, expect transport disruption on protest days and avoid demonstrations. Check FCDO travel advice for France.

sources.title: Euronews — France's third weekend of social protests
RTÉ — France braces for more unrest amid fresh protests

uk-rates.summary: UK CPI 3.5% and a Bank of England rate rise expected on 5 Nov
uk-rates.state: UK CPI inflation rose to 3.5% in September from 3.1%. Bank Rate is 3.75%, and money markets almost fully price a rise at the 5 Nov meeting, with further increases priced for February and July (Trading Economics, 30 Oct).
uk-rates.for_you: Mortgage rates are more likely to rise than fall in the coming months. Savings rates may also edge up.

sources.title: Trading Economics — UK 10-year gilt yield and BoE expectations

gilts.summary: Gilt yields ease after the Budget but stay near 19-year highs
gilts.state: The 10-year gilt yield was 5.29% at the 30 Oct close and the 30-year 5.72%, near multi-decade highs. Yields fell to their lowest since 22 Sep after Chancellor John Healey's first Budget met the fiscal rules. Markets reopen on 2 Nov ahead of the 5 Nov Bank of England decision.
gilts.for_you: Fixed-rate mortgage pricing tracks gilt yields, so new fixed deals remain expensive by recent standards.

sources.title: Trading Economics — UK 10-year gilt yield

uk-energy-cap.summary: Energy price cap forecast to rise about 25% in January
uk-energy-cap.state: The Ofgem cap for October to December is £1,723 a year for a typical dual-fuel household. Uswitch's average of British Gas, EDF and E.ON forecasts (updated 30 Oct) points to a 27% rise in January 2027, above the 20% Alert line, driven by the wholesale gas surge. Ofgem announces the January cap by 25 Nov.
uk-energy-cap.for_you: Household energy bills are likely to rise sharply from 1 January. Ofgem and Citizens Advice publish guidance on support if you're struggling to pay.

sources.title: Uswitch — Energy price cap January 2027 latest predictions
Energy Plus — Ofgem January 2027 price cap forecast

uk-weather.summary: No Met Office weather warnings in force
uk-weather.state: The Met Office had no weather warnings in force as of 11:40 UTC on 1 Nov, after yellow fog warnings earlier on 1 Nov expired. No amber or red warnings are in force.
uk-weather.for_you: No significant weather warnings at present. Check the Met Office forecast before travelling.

sources.title: Met Office — UK weather warnings

nhs-pressure.summary: Flu, COVID and RSV at low or baseline levels; flu usually rises in November
nhs-pressure.state: UKHSA's 29 Oct update (week 43) showed flu stable at low levels (6.6% positivity), COVID low and falling (8.3%), and RSV rising but at baseline. UKHSA notes flu usually picks up in November; the next update is due 5 Nov. Resident doctors in England strike from 14 to 19 Nov.
nhs-pressure.for_you: If eligible, get your flu and COVID vaccines before winter. Use NHS 111 for urgent but non-emergency care.

sources.title: GOV.UK — Latest UKHSA weekly winter virus surveillance data

uk-threat-level.summary: UK terrorism threat level raised to Severe: an attack is highly likely
uk-threat-level.state: The UK national terrorism threat level remains Severe, meaning an attack is highly likely, after MI5 raised it in October 2026. The MI5 Director General warned on 13 Oct of a rising threat from anti-migrant and anti-Muslim extremism alongside Islamist terrorism. No change as of 1 Nov.
uk-threat-level.for_you: Stay alert in crowded places and report anything suspicious via gov.uk/ACT or 999 in an emergency. Follow police and MI5 guidance.

sources.title: MI5 — UK national terrorism threat level raised to Severe
A News — UK faces rising threat from far-right terrorism, warns MI5 chief

uk-disruption.summary: Resident doctors strike 14–19 Nov; consultants plan two days
uk-disruption.state: The BMA has called a six-day strike by resident doctors in England from 14 to 19 Nov, and consultants have announced a two-day strike in November (NHS Employers). These are strikes in one sector, within the Watch band. No national infrastructure failure was reported as of 1 Nov.
uk-disruption.for_you: Attend appointments unless told otherwise. The NHS will contact you if yours is rescheduled. Use 111 or 999 as usual.

sources.title: NHS Employers — Consultant doctors announce strikes in November
Yahoo News — England's resident doctors to strike for six days
